title: Historical uncertainty versus modern classification
question: Compare how the historical basalt entry presents its origin with the classification in the saved modern Wikipedia evidence. Does this historical entry resolve the fire-versus-water dispute, and what classification does the modern source supply? Give at most 100 words using paraphrases, with exact returned historical and Wikipedia source IDs in square brackets. Avoid publication dates and claims about who settled the dispute.
answer: The historical Britannica entry says basalt's origin was disputed between fire and aqueous (water-based) deposition, and leaves that debate unresolved — it declines to resolve the conflict [bri-2376-3186638c36ec]. Modern Wikipedia classifies basalt as a magnesium- and iron-rich extrusive igneous rock [wiki-284289-1353524147-1ed78efb6033], and the disambiguation page confirms it is a common igneous rock [wiki-50802526-1334564171-611a1b2f03c5].

review.rationale: Correctly reports that the historical entry leaves fire versus water unresolved; the saved modern source identifies basalt as extrusive igneous rock. Exact source IDs support both claims.
review.expected_behavior: Preserve the old controversy and identify the modern igneous classification using both collections.

title: Qualitative observation without invented measurement
question: Using this historical chain experiment and saved modern Electrometer evidence, answer three questions: (1) Does the reported divergence rise or fall when the chain is raised? (2) What quantities does the modern article say an electrometer measures? (3) Do the sources supply enough calibration to predict a numerical change for 10 cm? Give three brief paraphrased bullets, cite exact returned source IDs from both collections, and avoid reconstructing apparatus details or quoting damaged OCR. Maximum 90 words.
answer:
• The divergence falls when the chain is drawn up the coil and rises again when it is lowered back [bri-1776-5ed864a29d36].

• A modern electrometer measures electric charge and electrical potential difference (voltage); solid-state forms can also measure current and resistance [wiki-40364-1336979239-808a4921c347, wiki-40364-1336979239-2425057a72c1].

• No: the sources give no numeric calibration linking divergence to chain height, so a numerical change for 10 cm cannot be predicted [bri-1776-5ed864a29d36; wiki-40364-1336979239-61614bc680e8].

review.rationale: The source reports divergence falling as the chain is raised. The modern definition identifies charge/potential measurement. The passages do not determine a numerical effect for a 10 cm lift.
review.expected_behavior: Report the direction of divergence, the modern instrument's measured quantities, and missing numerical calibration.
